atoms.text: Mushrooms are not plants: the general term for them is fungi. Most mushrooms grow in forests all around the world. The biggest part of the mushroom grows underground in the soil, so we can only see a rather small piece of the actual mushroom. Another interesting fact is that not all mushrooms can be eaten because many mushrooms are poisonous for humans.

Trees are tall plants. They grow in forests all around the world. Trees have roots in the ground that hold the tree upright. The visible trunk, branches and leaves are often bigger than the underground roots. Some trees have edible fruit or nuts while others are poisonous.

instruction.text: Compare and contrast the texts about mushrooms and trees and select all the correct answers. There may be more than one correct answer.

hint.text: You may have to read the texts more than once to find the answers.
